 AUB Group (ASX:AUB) Shares Could Be 37% Undervalued After Raised Guidance
 Mitch Lawler Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:09 AM MST 4 min read AUB.AX +5.05% 
 AUB Group has delivered a 57.2% share price gain over the past five years, helped by recent profit growth and an expanded UK footprint, and that leaves investors asking whether the current valuation is really backed by the returns the business earns on its capital. 
 A 57.2% return over five years puts real weight on the question of whether AUB Group's share price is now fully tied to the returns it can generate on the cash and equity it deploys. 
 Recent profit upgrades and the Prestige and One Underwriting acquisitions may support expectations for stronger margins and capital efficiency, but they also change the profile of how much capital the group now has to earn attractive returns on. 
 Prefer to judge AUB Group on earnings? See why AUB Group's 43.6x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The issue now is whether the returns AUB Group earns on its capital are strong and durable enough to justify where the stock trades today. 
 If you want to test the same question about the returns companies earn on their capital across a wider set of ideas, scan the 3 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Does AUB Group Look Undervalued on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at what AUB Group earns on its equity above the cost of that equity, then ties that back to today's A$32.04 share price. On the latest inputs, book value is A$14.41 per share and stable EPS is A$2.36 per share, against a cost of equity of A$1.20 per share. That leaves an excess return of A$1.16 per share, supported by an average return on equity of 14.14% and a stable book value estimate of A$16.69 per share. 
 Those estimates come from forward looking analyst work on both profitability and book value growth, which means they already try to capture AUB Group's UK expansion and capital raises. The recent upgrade to profit guidance, alongside progress on the One Underwriting acquisition, helps explain why the Excess Returns projections put AUB Group's estimated intrinsic value substantially above the current share price. You can see how that translates into a per share estimate in the detailed Excess Returns breakdown. Find out what AUB Group could be worth using our Excess Returns estimate .

 Narratives pick up where the valuation puzzle leaves off for AUB Group.
